source.title: The Cross-Architecture Substrate: A Domain-Transcendent, Calibration-Surviving Geometric Invariant of Modern Vision Encoders

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and checklist.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity and subspace overlap using its own PCA, CKA, calibration, and stitching procedures. It does not reproduce either original study’s full method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many application results that do not measure convergence or its predicted effects; these are omitted. Its proposed explanations involving shared training data or objectives are not experimentally disentangled. It does not compare models across parameter scales or capability levels, and its cross-modal tests are not paired image-caption tests.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-architecture, cross-objective, cross-domain and cross-modal representational alignment with its own PCA-substrate, PCKA and Gröger-calibrated CKA/mKNN methods. It also tests stitching, metric and K sensitivity, and alignment over training. It does not reproduce either original's method and has no model-scale sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim the substrate survives Gröger calibration and other published critiques, emerges in the first 10% of training, and stays within a modality. They argue that convergence belongs to the data-distribution-and-objective family (it is absent for biology models and the MAE paradigm), not to neural networks universally. They state the result is a direction-existence claim, not a shared coordinate system.
record.recipe_differences: Defines a joint PCA substrate and compares subspaces using PCKA and calibrated CKA, rather than reproducing either original source's method. It also tests alternative metrics, domains, and a stitching application.
record.method_sensitivity: PCKA rises with K from 0.55 at K=4 to 0.79 at K=64; four-domain to eight-domain median PCKA decreases from 0.679 to 0.604. The discriminative-versus-reconstruction ratio changes from 7.4× on ImageNette to 1.22× on the cross-domain panel. Grassmann mean cos² is low in absolute terms; orthogonal Procrustes disparity is nearly constant across pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Calibrated CKA works as a provenance fingerprint: same-family vs unrelated AUC 0.92, with clades recovered but not exact ancestry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity encodes architecture lineage and training-paradigm kind.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating named substrate PCs selectively degrades the classes that load on them, by 3–11× in vision and 27–72× in language.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared low-rank directions are causally used by the models.

record.code_released: not stated (paper says code and configs will be released upon acceptance; no URL stated)
record.problems: The central alignment magnitudes are explicitly described as panel-specific. Some reported results are aggregates over encoder pairs, and some measurements are described in text without uncertainty estimates. The paper's four-domain success-threshold statements are internally inconsistent: §3 says all six pairs exceed 0.50, while its matrix and Appendix D indicate one pair is 0.430 and only five of six exceed 0.50. Cross-modal tests are not paired image-caption comparisons; model size and capability scaling are not tested.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted application and forensic results that do not measure a claim version, including domain detection, low-shot probes, distillation, transfer prediction, and most provenance-classification results. The paper's cited results from other work were also excluded.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability between independently trained models; only training-progress (r18) and transfer-correlation (text) evidence.
Entirely untested: no paired image-caption alignment and no comparison as vision and language models improve.
No pure seed-only comparison; no test that individual units or bases differ while subspaces match.
Trained linear maps, layer stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested.
Recurrence of neurons, SAE features or circuits across same-modality models is not tested.

missing.what: Six-LLM, five-family panel: median calibrated PCKA 0.907 (min 0.834) at K=200, against a random-init null of 0.041
missing.versions: V7 (near-complete within-modality alignment); context for V1

missing.what: WikiText re-extraction gives median 0.907 at ℓ=L/4 and 0.886 at ℓ=3L/4, matching SST-2
Robustness attacks: ranking invariant across CKA/Procrustes/GULP/SVCCA (ρ 0.90–0.965); probe-n slope ≈0; 25/25 pairs pass the exact null
Cross-domain principal angles: literally shared fraction ≈0% at K=4 and 4.5% at K=16; subspace-CKA 0.02–0.04
A CLIP+CLAP vision-audio substrate fails the calibrated null; biology models vs vision/text give cal-CKA about 0.016
Substrate alignment vs transfer accuracy: τ=−0.08 over 14 encoders; stable-core τ=0.501; error ρ=−0.56 after removing MAE
Unanalysed size contrasts: Qwen3-8B is less aligned to the LLM panel than Qwen3-1.7B; ViT-L/16 aligns lower than ViT-B/16 with CNNs

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistencies: §3 says all six four-domain pairs exceed 0.50, while Appendix D shows 0.430 and 5/6. The abstract says all 14 encoders, including MAE, converge, yet the MAE controls align only 0.116. r5–r6 measure the stability of a joint panel subspace across input domains, not model-to-model alignment. Several cited works carry 2026 arXiv numbers, and code is not released.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep relating model size or capability to alignment between independently trained models.
No paired image-caption alignment test and no comparison of cross-modal alignment as vision and language models improve.
Does not test whether individual units or bases match; its reported seed/recipe result is a calibrated similarity comparison.
Tests orthogonal Procrustes head stitching on substrate scores, not layer stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping methods.
Tests correspondence of named axes across vision and language substrates, not recurrence of neurons, SAE features, or circuits across same-modality models.
Tests several similarity metrics, K settings, and visual domains, but not a broad range of neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution language inputs.
The study discusses shared data/objectives as possible explanations but does not isolate their causal contributions or compare against a common-reality explanation.

rows.subject: ResNet-50 trained from random initialization on ImageNette
rows.operation_detail: Tracked linear CKA between penultimate features and a fixed K=16 panel-substrate target during training.
rows.measure: CKA to fixed substrate target; validation top-1 accuracy
rows.value: CKA 0.58 by epoch 5, then 0.50–0.58 for the remaining 45 epochs; accuracy rises from 46% at epoch 5 to 76% at epoch 50
rows.locator: §6, Mechanism: Emergence in the First 10% of Training
rows.note: This is alignment to a fixed target during one model's training, not a sweep across model sizes or independently trained model pairs.
rows.check: For V7 the state is observed: alignment plateaus at 0.50–0.58 and stays far from 1. For V1 it is absent: alignment to the other-architecture panel substrate does not rise as accuracy climbs from 46% to 76%. This is training progress, not scale.

source_check.correct: V7 state observed. V1 state cannot_determine: this is a fixed-size model's training trajectory against a fixed target, not convergence with model scale across independently trained models.
source_check.problem: Observed is appropriate for V7's plateau, but this experiment does not measure V1's model-scale trend.
